'''Samuel B. Mukasa''' is a [[geochemist]] and academic administrator. He is a former executive vice president and provost of the [[SUNY College of Environmental Science and Forestry]] (SUNY ESF) and a professor emeritus at the [[University of Minnesota]].<ref name="AAS">{{cite web |title=Prof. Samuel B Mukasa |url=https://aasciences.africa/fellows/samuel-b-mukasa |website=African Academy of Sciences |access-date=26 October 2026}}</ref><ref name="UMNemeritus">{{cite web |title=Samuel B. Mukasa |url=https://cse.umn.edu/esci/samuel-b-mukasa |website=University of Minnesota |access-date=26 October 2026}}</ref>

Mukasa previously served as dean of the College of Science and Engineering at the University of Minnesota, dean of the College of Engineering and Physical Sciences at the [[University of New Hampshire]], and chair of the Department of Geological Sciences at the [[University of Michigan]].<ref name="AAS" /> He was president of the [[Geochemical Society]] from 2010 to 2011 and was elected a fellow of the [[African Academy of Sciences]] in 2023.<ref name="UMNdean">{{cite web |title=U appoints Samuel Mukasa as dean of College of Science and Engineering |url=https://twin-cities.umn.edu/news-events/u-appoints-samuel-mukasa-dean-college-science-and-engineering |website=University of Minnesota |date=14 June 2016 |access-date=26 October 2026}}</ref><ref name="GeochemPres">{{cite web |title=Past Presidents |url=https://geochemsoc.org/about/committees-and-personnel/archive/past-presidents |website=Geochemical Society |access-date=26 October 2026}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Mukasa was born in [[Kenya]] to [[Uganda]]n parents.<ref name="AAS"/> He received a bachelor's degree in geology from the [[University of New Hampshire]] in 1977 and a master's degree in geology from [[Ohio State University]] in 1980. He earned a PhD in geochemistry from the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]], in 1984. He completed postdoctoral research at the [[Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory]] of [[Columbia University]].<ref name="UMNdean"/><ref name="ESFappointment">{{cite web |title=Dr. Samuel B. Mukasa Joins ESF as Executive Vice President and Provost |url=https://www.esf.edu/news/2021/mukasa-joins-esf.php |website=SUNY College of Environmental Science and Forestry |date=1 November 2021 |access-date=26 October 2026}}</ref>

== Academic career ==
From 1985 to 1989, Mukasa was an assistant professor in the Department of Geology at the [[University of Florida]]. He joined the University of Michigan in 1989 and remained on its faculty for 21 years.<ref name="AAS" /> From 2007 to 2010, he chaired the Department of Geological Sciences, later renamed the Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences. In 2008, he was appointed the Eric J. Essene Collegiate Professor of Geological Sciences.<ref name="UMNdean"/><ref name="Michigan">{{cite report |title=Recommendation for Appointment of Samuel B. Mukasa as Eric J. Essene Collegiate Professor of Geological Sciences |url=https://regents.umich.edu/meetings/09-08/2008-09-IV-1-9.pdf |publisher=University of Michigan Board of Regents |date=September 2008 |access-date=26 October 2026}}</ref>

Mukasa moved to the University of New Hampshire in 2010 and served as dean of its College of Engineering and Physical Sciences from 2011 to 2016.<ref name="UMNdean"/><ref name="ESFappointment"/>

Mukasa became dean of the College of Science and Engineering at the University of Minnesota in August 2016.<ref name="ESFappointment" /> He held the position until 2021.<ref name="UMNdeans">{{cite web |title=College of Science and Engineering Deans, 1935 to present |url=https://cse.umn.edu/college/about/college-science-and-engineering-deans-1935-present |website=University of Minnesota |access-date=26 October 2026}}</ref>

In November 2021, Mukasa was appointed executive vice president and provost of SUNY ESF.<ref name="ESFappointment"/> His appointment was also reported by ''[[The Journal of Blacks in Higher Education]]''.<ref name="JBHE">{{cite news |title=Samuel Mukasa Is the New Provost at SUNY's College of Environmental Science and Forestry |url=https://jbhe.com/2021/11/samuel-mukasa-is-the-new-provost-at-sunys-college-of-environmental-science-and-forestry/ |work=The Journal of Blacks in Higher Education |date=8 November 2021 |access-date=26 October 2026}}</ref> He was granted provost emeritus status effective January 1, 2025.<ref name="ESFemeritus">{{cite report |title=Personnel Actions Presented for Board Endorsement |url=https://www.esf.edu/trustees/documents/2024/personnel-action-12062024.pdf |publisher=SUNY College of Environmental Science and Forestry |date=6 December 2024 |access-date=26 October 2026}}</ref>

Mukasa served as president of the [[Geochemical Society]] from 2010 to 2011.<ref name="GeochemPres" /> He also served as an associate editor of the ''[[Geological Society of America Bulletin]]'' from 1995 to 1998.<ref name="ESFappointment" />

== Research ==
Mukasa's research has examined the chemical composition and geological evolution of the Earth's [[mantle (geology)|mantle]] and [[Earth's crust|crust]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sam Mukasa {{!}} U-M LSA Earth and Environmental Sciences |url=https://lsa.umich.edu/earth/people/emeritus-faculty/mukasa.html |access-date=2026-10-26 |website=lsa.umich.edu |language=en}}</ref> His work uses trace-element analysis and radiogenic isotope systems, including lead, neodymium, strontium, hafnium, and osmium, to investigate the origins of [[igneous rock]]s and geological processes associated with [[plate tectonics]]. He has also employed [[uranium–lead dating]] and [[argon–argon dating]] to investigate the timing of geological events.<ref name="AAS"/><ref name="ESFappointment"/>

In a 1987 study published in ''[[Geology (journal)|Geology]]'', Mukasa and John N. Ludden used uranium–lead dating of zircon crystals from the [[Troodos Ophiolite]] in Cyprus to constrain the age of its formation.<ref name="Troodos" /> Their analysis yielded an estimated crystallization age of approximately 91.6 million years for plagiogranite samples, providing evidence about the timing of oceanic crust formation in the eastern Mediterranean.<ref name="Troodos">{{Cite journal |last=Mukasa |first=Samuel B. |last2=Ludden |first2=John N. |date=1987-09-01 |title=Uranium-lead isotopic ages of plagiogranites from the Troodos ophiolite, Cyprus, and their tectonic significance |url=https://doi.org/10.1130/0091-7613(1987)152.0.CO;2 |journal=Geology |volume=15 |issue=9 |pages=825–828 |doi=10.1130/0091-7613(1987)15<825:UIAOPF>2.0.CO;2 |issn=0091-7613|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Mukasa also co-authored research on mantle metasomatism, including a 2002 study of peridotite xenoliths from [[Spitsbergen]]. Published in the ''[[Journal of Petrology]]'', the study examined the chemical effects of interactions between mantle rocks and migrating melts, using trace-element compositions and numerical modelling.<ref name="Ionov">{{Cite journal |last=IONOV |first=DMITRI A. |last2=BODINIER |first2=JEAN-LOUIS |last3=MUKASA |first3=SAMUEL B. |last4=ZANETTI |first4=ALBERTO |date=2002-12-01 |title=Mechanisms and Sources of Mantle Metasomatism: Major and Trace Element Compositions of Peridotite Xenoliths from Spitsbergen in the Context of Numerical Modelling |url=https://doi.org/10.1093/petrology/43.12.2219 |journal=Journal of Petrology |volume=43 |issue=12 |pages=2219–2259 |doi=10.1093/petrology/43.12.2219 |issn=0022-3530|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

A substantial part of Mukasa's research has concerned Antarctica, particularly the geological history of [[Marie Byrd Land]], the [[West Antarctic Rift System]], and the relationship between Antarctic magmatism and the breakup of [[Gondwana]].<ref name="AAS" /><ref name="ESFappointment" /> He co-authored a 1994 study examining the relationship between Antarctica–New Zealand rifting, magmatism in Marie Byrd Land, and mantle processes. The study proposed links between mid-Cretaceous magmatism, ridge subduction, and mantle plume activity.<ref name="Weaver">{{Cite journal |last=Weaver |first=S. D. |last2=Storey |first2=B. C. |last3=Pankhurst |first3=R. J. |last4=Mukasa |first4=S. B. |last5=DiVenere |first5=V. J. |last6=Bradshaw |first6=J. D. |date=1994-09-01 |title=Antarctica-New Zealand rifting and Marie Byrd Land lithospheric magmatism linked to ridge subduction and mantle plume activity |url=https://doi.org/10.1130/0091-7613(1994)0222.3.CO;2 |journal=Geology |volume=22 |issue=9 |pages=811–814 |doi=10.1130/0091-7613(1994)022<0811:ANZRAM>2.3.CO;2 |issn=0091-7613|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In a 2000 paper with [[Ian Dalziel (geologist)|Ian Dalziel]], Mukasa investigated the geological evolution of West Antarctica's Pacific margin using zircon uranium–lead geochronology and feldspar lead-isotope data. The research examined the timing and geological development of Marie Byrd Land within the broader history of Gondwana.<ref name="Dalziel">{{Cite journal |last=Mukasa |first=S. B. |last2=Dalziel |first2=I. W. D. |date=2000-04-01 |title=Marie Byrd Land, West Antarctica: Evolution of Gondwana's Pacific margin constrained by zircon U-Pb geochronology and feldspar common-Pb isotopic compositions |url=https://doi.org/10.1130/0016-7606(2000)112<611:mblwae>2.0.co;2 |journal=Geological Society of America Bulletin |volume=112 |issue=4 |pages=611–627 |doi=10.1130/0016-7606(2000)112<611:mblwae>2.0.co;2 |issn=0016-7606|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In a 2020 study published in the ''[[Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth]]'', he and his co-authors analyzed submarine basalt samples dredged from the Chukchi Borderland in the western Arctic Ocean. Using argon–argon geochronology, major- and trace-element analysis, and isotope geochemistry, the researchers examined the origins and timing of volcanic activity associated with the geological development of the Amerasia Basin. The study identified several episodes of Cretaceous volcanic activity and considered their implications for tectonic models of Arctic Ocean basin formation.<ref name="Chukchi">{{Cite journal |last=Mukasa |first=Samuel B. |last2=Andronikov |first2=Alexandre |last3=Brumley |first3=Kelley |last4=Mayer |first4=Larry A. |last5=Armstrong |first5=Andrew |date=2020-07-01 |title=Basalts From the Chukchi Borderland: 40Ar/39Ar Ages and Geochemistry of Submarine Intraplate Lavas Dredged From the Western Arctic Ocean |url=https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1029/2019JB017604 |journal=Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth |language=en |publisher=John Wiley & Sons, Ltd |volume=125 |issue=7 |pages= |doi=10.1029/2019JB017604 |issn=2169-9356}}</ref>

== Honors and recognition ==
Mukasa was elected a fellow of the [[Geological Society of America]] in 2004 and is also a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]. He was elected to the [[African Academy of Sciences]] in 2023.<ref name="AAS" /><ref name="UMNdean" /><ref name="GSA">{{cite web |title=Active & Current Fellows |url=https://www.geosociety.org/what-we-do/honors-awards/fellowship/current-fellows |website=Geological Society of America |access-date=26 October 2026}}</ref>

He received a distinguished alumnus award from the University of California, Santa Barbara in 2006 and an honorary doctorate from [[Nkumba University]] in Uganda in 2008.<ref name="ESFappointment"/>
